record.paper_title: Answering open questions in biology using spatial genomics and structured methods
record.original_question: How do cell state and gene-expression profiles interact with cellular morphology, movement, and behavior, including both directions of influence in which gene expression shapes morphology and motion while changes in morphology and motion feed back to alter gene expression?

evidence.quote: 2 How does cell state and expression profile interact with cellular morphology, movement, and behavior?

Biologically, cell morphology and movement are determined largely by membrane contacts; cell membranes are predominantly composed of lipids and proteins, and the abundances of these components are largely dictated by gene expression. However, changes in morphology and motion also drive changes in gene expression as the cell responds to new conditions.

artifact.category_tag: cell morphology and gene expression coupling
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a living cell modeled as a dynamical system characterized by two coupled state descriptors: (i) a high-dimensional gene-expression / cell-state profile e(t) ∈ R^n (e.g. transcript abundances across n genes, together with discrete or continuous cell-type labels), and (ii) a morphological/behavioral descriptor m(t) (e.g. cell shape parameters, membrane geometry, polarity, and instantaneous velocity / migratory behavior). Biologically, membrane composition — largely lipids and proteins whose abundances are controlled by gene expression — strongly constrains m(t), while changes in m(t) (shape deformation, motion, mechanical environment) feed back to alter e(t).

Formulate and characterize the bidirectional coupling between e(t) and m(t). Specifically:

1. Identify which components of the gene-expression profile e(t) causally determine which features of cellular morphology, membrane dynamics, and motile behavior m(t), and quantify the corresponding forward map e ↦ m.

2. Identify how perturbations to morphology and motion (changes in m(t), including mechanical stresses, shape changes, and migration through different environments) feed back to alter gene expression, and quantify the corresponding reverse map m ↦ e.

3. Combine (1) and (2) into a coupled model (e.g. of the form de/dt = F(e,m), dm/dt = G(e,m)) whose predictions agree with experimental observations across diverse cell types and conditions.

Provide a complete mechanistic and predictive account of this bidirectional interaction.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad open biological research question about coupling between gene expression and cell morphology/behavior. No general solution exists; it remains an active area of investigation in cell biology and spatial genomics.

status_evidence.title: Spatial genomics overview
status_evidence.snippet: Spatial transcriptomics and morphology-coupled analyses are an emerging, unresolved area of study.
status_evidence.claim: The interaction between cell state/expression and morphology/behavior remains an active open problem.
